findings.title: Top-events queries select different aggregates with the same alias
findings.description:
Only `timeseries_columns` is transformed; `selected_columns` still comes directly from the request. For a normal top-events request with `field=count()` and `yAxis=count()`, `TopEventsQueryBuilder.__init__` combines the original `count()` with `upsampled_count() as count`. Both resolve to the alias `count`, despite computing different values, producing conflicting selected expressions.

The initial top-N selection also continues ranking by raw event counts, so projects or groups with different sampling rates can return the wrong top series even after the alias conflict is fixed.

Apply upsampling consistently to the ranking fields, ordering, and timeseries aggregates, preserving distinct aliases where needed. Add a top-events integration test with differing sampling rates.

findings.title: Input-format alias transformation makes upsampled series serialize as zero
findings.description:
With `transformAliasToInputFormat=1`, `BaseQueryBuilder.process_results` renames the returned `count` key to the supplied expression, `upsampled_count() as count`. However, `OrganizationEventsV2EndpointBase.get_event_stats_data` still resolves the requested axis from the original `count()`.

Consequently, `SnubaTSResultSerializer.serialize` looks up `count()` in rows containing `upsampled_count() as count` and falls back to zero. Eligible requests therefore return zero-valued series even when events exist.

Preserve the original public axis name through result processing, or translate transformed results back before serialization. Cover both single-axis and multi-axis requests with this flag enabled.

findings.title: Substring matching does not establish an errors-only query
findings.description:
Checking whether the raw query contains `event.type:error` also accepts `!event.type:error`, `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, and quoted text containing that substring. These queries do not restrict Discover results to errors, yet eligible projects will have their counts replaced by the error-specific weighted aggregate.

This violates the helper’s errors-only contract and can produce incorrect counts or unsupported cross-dataset queries. Determine eligibility from parsed search conditions, accounting for negation and boolean operators, and leave ambiguous queries untransformed. Add negative tests for negated filters, mixed-type OR expressions, and quoted text.
